record.original_question: Can the Lavrentiev phenomenon occur in elastostatics under growth assumptions on the stored-energy function that force every finite-energy deformation to be continuous, including for mixed boundary conditions or interior singularities?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Can the Lavrentiev phenomenon occur for elastostatics under growth conditions on the stored-energy function ensuring that all finite-energy deformations are continuous?
Whether such examples can be constructed for mixed boundary conditions of the type (2.1), even in two dimensions, or be associated with singularities in the interior of Ω, remains open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, and let $W:\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+\to[0,\infty)$ be a stored-energy function (where $\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}_+$ denotes matrices with positive determinant). Assume $W$ satisfies growth conditions strong enough to ensure that every deformation $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ with finite total energy
$$E(u)=\int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx<\infty$$
is (Hölder) continuous on $\overline\Omega$; e.g.\ $W(F)\ge c|F|^p$ for some $p>n$, possibly together with polyconvexity, frame indifference, isotropy, and $W(F)\to\infty$ as $\det F\to 0^+$.

Consider the variational problem of minimizing $E(u)$ over an admissible class $\mathcal{A}$ of deformations satisfying prescribed boundary or topological constraints. The Lavrentiev phenomenon is said to occur if
$$\inf_{u\in\mathcal{A}}E(u)\ <\ \inf_{u\in\mathcal{A}\cap C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)}E(u),$$
i.e.\ if smooth admissible deformations cannot approximate the infimum in energy.

Question: Under such continuity-forcing growth conditions on $W$, can the Lavrentiev phenomenon occur in elastostatics, in particular:
(a) for the problem with mixed displacement/traction (Dirichlet–Neumann) boundary conditions on disjoint portions of $\partial\Omega$, even in two space dimensions; and
(b) when the energy concentration causing the gap is associated with a singularity in the interior of $\Omega$ rather than on the boundary?
artifact.status_search_result: The basic question—whether the Lavrentiev phenomenon can occur in elastostatics under growth conditions forcing finite-energy deformations to be continuous—has been answered affirmatively: a 2D example with smooth, polyconvex, frame-indifferent, isotropic stored-energy density of p>2 growth, with W(F)→∞ as det F→0+, was constructed (2023), and further neo-Hookean examples in 2D and 3D exhibiting a Lavrentiev gap with continuous a.e.-injective deformations have appeared. The refinements concerning mixed boundary conditions and interior singularities are addressed in part by the neo-Hookean dipole-type singularity construction in 3D, but the original mixed-boundary-condition variant (in particular in 2D) does not appear fully resolved in the literature, so the overall problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: A new example for the Lavrentiev phenomenon in nonlinear elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth polyconvex frame-indifferent isotropic energy with p>2 growth and W(F)→∞ as det F→0+ exhibiting Lavrentiev gap in 2D, with continuous finite-energy deformations.
status_evidence.claim: Gives an affirmative answer to the question whether Lavrentiev phenomenon can occur under growth conditions forcing continuity.

status_evidence.title: A Lavrentiev phenomenon in the neo-Hookean model
status_evidence.snippet: Lavrentiev gap for neo-Hookean energy in 3D nonlinear elasticity, with mechanism a dipole-type interior singularity, deformations continuous and a.e. injective.
status_evidence.claim: Provides example involving interior singularity, addressing part (b).

status_evidence.title: The Lavrentiev Gap Phenomenon in Nonlinear Elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier work on Lavrentiev gap in nonlinear elasticity.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the problem in the elasticity setting.
